label: The 0600 file backend is readable by every bot child: the store sits under the user state root and every executor runs as the same OS user with unrestricted reads, so the `secrets:` grant is injection-only, not read-isolation. Add the same-user trust boundary to §6 and either accept it or isolate the store; test an undeclared bot reading another value.

The `[REMEMBER]` proposal fact is never checked for secret literals; T020 checks only the rendered block, so a child can print `[REMEMBER] token ghp_...` and the value lands in the item file and `bots inbox`. Check the fact with findSecretLiteral before writing the item and refuse `memory-proposal-secret`.

Two phases edit the same needs-you item shape with different fields (`kind`/`proposal` vs `grants`) and only 005 defines a missing-field default; a parallel build merges two shapes and pre-phase items fail one. Define item v2 once, have 006 cite it, and add a missing-`grants` default beside 005's `kind` default.

`bots remember` does not check the fact it appends, so one secret written by an operator poisons the block and the dispatch-time check refuses every later run. Refuse `memory-entry-secret` at append time and keep the dispatch check as the second line.

The apps filter is a capability filter for the Code Mode server, not a security boundary: a shell-capable bot can read `.utcp_config.json` and call any server. Add one line to §6/§7 stating what the filter does not close.

reason: Every named path and line resolves; the two missing items are create tasks.
